text:
Mia Chen: quick handoff — I'm primary until 22:00 PT, handing to Noah. Ongoing: elevated tail latency + a small 502 spike this evening from runtime-proxy in us-west-2. Pager alerts: inference-5xx-rate > 1% over last 12m, kv-cache queue depth high for model-pool-3. IncidentBot: SEV2 alert raised at 2145675200.

Mia Chen: SUMMARY:
- Impact: some streaming/generation requests get 502 or long hangs (~3-6s extra) for customers hitting high batch sizes. Not widespread; affecting ~0.7% of requests overall but concentrated on a few heavy-traffic customers in US west. EU region unaffected.
- Root suspicion: cache eviction thrashing + one worker host (gpu-12) showing memory pressure.
- Mitigations in progress: autoscaler +4 replicas (from 8 -> 12) applied, fallback route to model v1-small enabled for tiered routing, temporary TTL reduction on prefix cache to reduce hot-key churn.

Mia Chen: Current state / what I did so far:
- Scaled model-pool-3 deployment: `kubectl scale deploy/model-pool-3 --replicas=12 -n runtime` (succeeded)
- Enabled routing fallback: set `route_policy.fallback = v1-small` for us-west-2 in runtime-config (changed via console, immediate).
- Applied cache TTL tweak: `redis-cli -h kv-cache-master config set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru` and reduced TTL on hot-prefix to 30s (temporary).
- Identified host gpu-12 with oom_kill churn; cordoned and drained it: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets` — still investigating why its KV eviction increased.

Mia Chen: Open items I couldn't finish before handoff:
- Need someone to keep an eye on the autoscaler — it may undershoot because pod startup time for that model is ~45s. If queue depth stays > 400 for >10m, we should bump replicas by another +4.
- Check kdump logs on gpu-12 (needs infra access, I started a collection but didn't fully pull logs).
- Run a canary traffic test on fallback route to confirm behavioral parity for the heavy customers (Noah can run if you have curl snippets).

Mia Chen: runbook refs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions and https://console.redwood.ai/routing/playbooks/fallbacks — playbook commands below.

Mia Chen: emergency commands (copied):
```
# scale up quickly
kubectl scale deploy/model-pool-3 --replicas=16 -n runtime
# force route to small model for customer X
redwoodctl routing set --region us-west-2 --route inference.customer-X --model v1-small
# drain problematic node
kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=10m
```

Noah Patel: acked. I'll take primary from you at 22:00 PT. Quick questions: the fallback to v1-small — is that global or only for the overflow route?

Mia Chen: it's region-scoped (us-west-2) and only for the overflow/latency-policy routes right now, not a global model swap. I set it via the routing policy so it's targeted.

Noah Patel: ok. I'll watch autoscaler and logs. If queue depth stays > 400 for 15m, I'll scale to 16 and open a short-lived canary to validate. Can you paste the canary curl?

Mia Chen: canary curl for streaming (example):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"v1-small","input":"tokenized test","stream":true}' \
  https://us-west-2.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Expect short bursts; if we see matching outputs but with lower latency, fallback is good.

Sanjay Kapoor: I'm secondary. If this escalates to SEV1, I'll take over paging and coordinate with infra. I can pick up gpu-12 investigation (I have HSM access and node logs perms). Noted that a kernel patch went out last week to gpu hosts — could be related.

Tess Rivera: FYI there's a maintenance window scheduled for us-west-2 at 03:30 UTC tomorrow (non-disruptive per SRE notes) but double-check since our drain might interact. I put a note on the maintenance board.

Mia Chen: customer impact details (for handoff):
- Affected customers: Cust-A (15% of their requests), Cust-B (sporadic errors during heavy-batch windows).
- Observability: dashboard `prod -> inference -> error-rate` has a temporary filter `service:runtime-proxy, region:us-west-2`. Use that to eyeball.

IncidentBot: Pager escalated to SEV2 (2145675200) — active alerts: inference-5xx-rate (us-west-2), kv-cache-queue-depth, runtime-host-oom.

InfraBot: node gpu-12 shows dmesg OOM events at 2145674800 and 2145675300 — collection in progress.

Noah Patel: I'll start by running the canary and watching logs for 10m, then decide on another scale. If we need to ramp to 20 replicas, we'll coordinate with infra for GPU allocation.

Sanjay Kapoor: on gpu-12: I'll try to pull `/var/log/messages` and `dmesg` after you hand over. If it's kernel-related, we can rollback last week's kernel package on that node image and reprovision. Warn: rollback requires host restart — plan for a quick maintenance swap.

Mia Chen: coverage note: after my shift ends at 22:00 PT and Noah takes over, there will be a gap between 02:00-06:00 UTC with no dedicated infra oncall (we tried to get coverage but couldn't). If the issue starts recurring there, escalate to oncall-leads and I'll try to be reachable.

Noah Patel: acknowledged. I'll update this thread on any state changes. If anyone sees `error-rate > 2%` or `queue-depth > 800`, ping me `@Noah` and I'll wake Sanjay.

Mia Chen: handing off now — all control-plane changes recorded in audit log `audit-2145678`. TL;DR: scaled + routing fallback + cache TTL tweak. Keep an eye on gpu-12 and autoscaler. :eyes: :warning:

Noah Patel: taking primary. Thanks Mia — good notes.

Mia Chen: thanks team, leaving channel.

Noah Patel: (added) starting monitoring window now. Will post an update at +30m and again at +2h unless something critical happens.

PagerBot: Reaction summary: :eyes: x3, :thumbsup: x2 on latest status update.
